questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How schools teach the science of climate change to young children
The life story of Greta Thunberg
Why politicians disagree about climate policy
Young people's climate fears and how adults can talk to them about it
questions.why: They ask whether talking honestly about the climate can help mend divisions between generations.

questions.q: What did one recent survey show about young people in the UK?
options: At least three-quarters find the future frightening
Most of them have never heard about climate change at all
About half want to become climate activists
Very few feel betrayed by adults
questions.why: Beth says three-quarters or more of young people in the UK feel the future is frightening.

questions.q: Why does Immie compare climate change to a parasite?
options: Because it only affects animals and plants, not human beings
Because it is caused by lazy people
Because it keeps growing while everything else dies
Because scientists can't see it
questions.why: She says it's the only thing growing and getting bigger while everything else dies off.

questions.q: What point does Milly make about the planet?
options: Humans could easily move to another planet one day
It is very special and we have nowhere else to go
It will recover on its own in time
Only rich countries can protect it
questions.why: She says if we get rid of the environment, “there's nowhere else we can go”.

questions.q: What has psychotherapist Caroline Hickman done?
options: Started a school strike for the climate in Stockholm
Talked to over 100,000 teenagers in 10 countries
Written a law about climate education
Surveyed parents in the UK only
questions.why: Neil says she visited 10 countries, talking to over 100,000 teenagers about their climate fears.

questions.q: What did the teenagers tell Caroline about adults?
options: Adults were too frightened to go outside
Adults happily talked with them about the climate every day
Adults ignored them or said fixing the planet was their job
Adults were leading most climate protests
questions.why: They mentioned parents ignoring them and adults saying, “Fixing the planet is your job now!”

questions.q: What is Caroline's main advice to parents and teachers?
options: Talk about it often, not in one big conversation
Wait until children are older before discussing it
Avoid the subject so children don't get upset
Give children all the answers from experts
questions.why: She says don't put it off or save it up for one big conversation – talk about it regularly.

questions.q: What does Caroline suggest by telling adults to say “let's find out together”?
options: Children should solve the problem on their own
Parents must become climate scientists before they talk about it
Talking about climate is a waste of time
Adults don't need to know everything to have an honest talk
questions.why: She says it's OK to admit “I don't have all the answers” and work it out together.
